prompt:
Create `merge_customers.py` (Python 3.12 standard library only) that merges customer records from the CRM export (`data/crm.csv`) and the billing export (`data/billing.json`) into one golden record per person. See README.md and the sample files for the input formats.

Common record shape used everywhere below: a dict with keys `source` (`"crm"` or `"billing"`), `id` (str), `name`, `email`, `phone`, `city` (raw strings, `""` when missing) and `updated_at` (a timezone-aware `datetime`).

Implement:
- `normalize_email(raw) -> str | None`: strip and lowercase. It must contain exactly one `@` with a non-empty part on each side, else `None`. Drop everything from the first `+` in the local part. If the domain is `gmail.com` or `googlemail.com`, also remove every `.` from the local part and use the domain `gmail.com`. If the local part ends up empty, return `None`. `None` or blank input returns `None`.
- `normalize_phone(raw) -> str | None`: keep only the digits. If they start with `00`, drop those two zeros. If exactly 10 digits remain, put `1` in front. A result with 11 to 15 digits is returned as `"+" + digits`; anything else (including `None` input) returns `None`.
- `load_crm(path) -> list[dict]`: CSV with header `crm_id,name,email,phone,city,updated_at`.
- `load_billing(path) -> list[dict]`: a JSON list of objects `{"billing_id", "full_name", "contact": {"email", "phone"}, "address": {"city"}, "last_modified"}`; `contact` or `address` (or keys inside them) may be missing or `null`, which means `""`.
  For both loaders: timestamps are ISO-8601 (a space or `T` separator; `Z`, an offset, or no offset, which means UTC); `id` comes from `crm_id` / `billing_id`; `name` from `name` / `full_name`. `path` may be `str` or `Path`.
- `merge(records) -> list[dict]`:
  - Two records belong to the same person when their normalised emails are equal (and not `None`) or their normalised phones are equal (and not `None`). Matching is transitive (A~B and B~C puts A, B, C together) and works within and across sources.
  - For each person, output `{"ids", "name", "email", "phone", "city", "updated_at"}`:
    - `ids`: sorted list of `"<source>:<id>"` strings;
    - each of `name`, `email`, `phone`, `city`: taken from the highest-priority record that has a value for it. Priority: latest `updated_at` first (compare instants); on a tie, `crm` before `billing`; then the lexicographically smaller `id`. "Has a value": for `email`/`phone` the normalised value is not `None` (output the normalised value); for `name`/`city` the value is non-empty after stripping (output it stripped). `None` when no record has a value;
    - `updated_at`: the latest `updated_at` of the group in UTC, formatted `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.
  - Sort the output by the first element of `ids`.
- Command line: `python merge_customers.py --crm CRM_CSV --billing BILLING_JSON --out OUT_JSON` loads both files, merges all records, and writes the merged list as JSON to OUT_JSON.
